trial_court: Family Court, Dhenkanal in C.P. Case No. 54 of 2018
facts_of_case: Appellant and Respondent No.1 got married, but Respondent No.1 filed an application under Section 7 Explanation(b) of the Family Court Act, 1984 to declare that the marriage certificate is nonest in the eye of law and she is not the wife of Appellant.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to set aside a registered marriage to prove that the registration was obtained through fraud, coercion, or undue influence.
legal_principles.held: Taking into consideration the respective pleas and the evidence on record, the Court below observed that both parties are Hindus and it is admitted fact that their marriage was registered at AMOFOI Organisation and accordingly said marriage certificate was issued by that organization.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not lightly set aside a registered marriage without sufficient evidence to support the claim.
legal_principles.held: No document was filed by respondent No.2 to show that their organization has got authority to perform the marriage.

outcome.final_order: The trial court declared that the marriage certificate issued by Respondent No.2's Organisation (AMOFOI) is nonest in the eye of law and Respondent No.1 is not the legally married wife of Appellant.
